title: Quality assurance and process-outcome research in psychodynamic child and adolescent psychotherapy
summary: The QVA-KJ project links psychotherapeutic quality assurance and practice-based psychotherapy research, and aims to establish both an IT-based quality assurance system oriented on the needs of clinical practice and investigating indication criteria, process variables and long-term courses of outpatient psychodynamic psychotherapies with children and adolescents. For this purpose, patients, parents and therapists of the private practices and outpatient clinics participating in the project are automatically invited in regular intervals via an online portal to take part in questionnaire surveys, in which relevant aspects for the diagnostic assessment at the beginning of the psychotherapeutic treatment as well as changes in the long-term course are assessed using well-established questionnaires (e.g. symptom severity, levels of personality functioning, intrapsychic conflicts, defense mechanisms, quality of life). Therapists can download the results of the surveys directly from the QVA-KJ portal in form of a PDF report and use it for internal quality assurance. At the same time, the pseudonymized data contribute to the empirical investigation of long-term effectiveness, differential indications and process dynamics of psychodynamic therapies with children and adolescents. Irrespective of the duration of treatment, data are collected from all patients at three-month intervals over a period of 8 years. This also allows conclusions on the long-term effectiveness and long-term cost-effectiveness of the treatments carried out.
